prompt: Which form of business ownership represents the minority of business in the U S yet makes up the majority of sales?
explanation: Corporations. In the U.S., corporations are in the minority as a form of business ownership, but they also generate the majority of sales. There are many more sole proprietorships, partnerships, and LLCs in the U.S., but they do not generate near as many sales as corporations.

prompt: What are import quotas or tariffs designed to do?
choices: Prevent harmful substances from entering a country
Protect a countrys economy from foreign competition
Prevent illegal immigration across national borders
Eliminate the movement of illegal merchandise
explanation: Protect a country's economy from foreign competition. By imposing tariffs or quotas on commodities entering a country, the country can reduce the economic impact of imported products. Quotas or tariffs do not prevent harmful substances or illegal merchandise from entering a country. Quotas and tariffs do not have an impact on illegal immigration.

prompt: Two retailers compete with each other distributing the same product This is an example of __________ conflict
explanation: Horizontal. Two retailers competing is an example of horizontal conflict, or conflict between two members at the same level of a channel of distribution. Vertical conflict occurs between members at different levels of the same channel (e.g., a manufacturer and a wholesaler). Economic and distributive are not types of conflict in channels of distribution.

prompt: A channel of distribution ends when the product reaches its ultimate consumer or when
choices: changes are made to the product
an intermediary goes out of business
explanation: Changes are made to the product. A channel of distribution ends when the product reaches its ultimate consumer or when changes are made to the product (e.g., when flour becomes bread or when components become an engine). An intermediary may go out of business, but there will always be other intermediaries to step in and complete the channel. A channel does not end when it leaves the producer or reaches a wholesaler--it isn't over until the product reaches the consumer.

prompt: Warehouse management systems are mainly used to __________ while enterprise resource planning software provides __________
choices: manage supply chain customer service training
manage inventory automated processes across departments
keep costs low complex inventory optimization
integrate all management real time optimization information
explanation: Manage inventory; automated processes across departments. Warehouse management systems (WMS) and enterprise resource planning software (ERP) are both important to distribution and channel management, but they differ in functionality. The main purpose of WMS is to manage inventory, including tracking items as they are picked, packed, shipped, and received. WMS are generally stand-alone, meaning that they solely provide inventory management. On the other hand, ERP software automates business processes in various departments, including not only inventory management, but also many others, such as accounting and customer relationship management. Both WMS and ERP manage supply chain, and ERP software does not necessarily provide customer service training. WMS is not used primarily to keep costs low; in fact, it can be more expensive than other types of channel management technology. Also, WMS provides complex inventory training; ERP does not. WMS is not used to integrate all management; this is a function of ERP software. Finally, real-time optimization is a function of WMS rather than ERP software.

prompt: One of the worlds biggest technology companies only allows one type of Web browsing application to function on its devices This is an example of
explanation: A tying agreement. A tying agreement occurs when a channel member's product is exclusively tied to the mandatory purchase of another product. Tying agreements are illegal when they reduce competition or create monopolies. In this case, if one of the biggest technology companies only allows one type of Web browsing application to function on its devices, other Web browsing applications cannot fairly compete in the market. Therefore, it is a tying agreement. Full line forcing is when a producer or supplier insists that the dealer must carry the full range of products in a line. There is no indication that full line forcing is occurring here. Closed territories occur when producers restrict their distributors to certain geographic regions. That is not occurring in this case. Finally, intellectual property is any work or creation that is protected by rights, such as copyright, patent, or trademark rights.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an affinity partnership
choices: An airline offers frequent flyer miles to travelers
A credit card company offers cards with sports teams logos
A restaurant gives discounts to those who join its rewards program
A bank pays to have its name on a local concert venue
explanation: A credit card company offers cards with sports teams' logos. Affinity marketing is a strategy in which an organization solicits responses from a group that shares a common interest or activity. If a credit card has a sports team's logo on it, fans of that team might be more likely to choose that particular company. An airline that offers frequent flyer miles is not an affinity partnership because there is no relationship between the airline and another organization; rather, this is an example of frequency marketing. A restaurant giving discounts to members of its rewards program is also an example of a frequency marketing strategy. Finally, a bank that pays to have its name on a local concert venue is engaged in a sponsorship, rather than an affinity partnership.

prompt: Katie has developed a new product idea and plans to share it at the next staff meeting Katie knows that some coworkers will object to her idea When her coworkers share concerns that her idea wont work Katie should
choices: remind her coworkers that they are sharing opinions not facts
explain that there is no proof her idea wouldnt work
acknowledge their concerns and respond in a respectful manner
repeat her proposal because it is based on quality research
explanation: Acknowledge their concerns and respond in a respectful manner. To objectively defend an idea, it is important to acknowledge any concerns, consider them, and respond in a respectful manner. Stating that there is no proof that the idea wouldn't work does little to defend the idea and does not demonstrate an objective attitude. While it may be true that Katie's coworkers are only sharing opinions, their opinions may be based on years of experience and should be considered. Information based on quality research can provide good insight, but repeating the information does little to defend against concerns and does not demonstrate objectivity.

prompt: To take effective written notes during a presentation its important to
choices: write down everything that the presenter says and does
write the notes in your own words
clearly understand the information before writing it down
explanation: Write the notes in your own words. It is important to write the notes in your own words whenever possible so you can easily understand them later. It is impossible to write down everything a presenter says and does; words, phrases, and abbreviations should be used to take notes quickly. It's not likely that you will understand everything presented, but by taking good notes you can review them later to gain understanding or to study further. Using good grammar and spelling in your notes is helpful but not essential, since they are only meant for your use.

prompt: Digital communications such as email may put a business at more risk than memos or letters stored as paper records because
choices: email users may use slang or make embarrassing remarks
email users may make careless spelling errors
email communications are more difficult to secure
explanation: Email communications are more difficult to secure. Email messages can be intercepted by unscrupulous people in a number of different ways, both physically (if either the sending or receiving device is stolen or lacking effective security features) and digitally (such as through hacking). Paper records, on the other hand, can be more easily protected using locked, fireproof cabinets and other physical storage. Poor spelling, slang, and inappropriate remarks can occur in any form of communication or documentation and should be avoided. Any business communication can contain confidential information, but the inability to effectively secure email puts any private information contained in email messages at risk.

prompt: While attending a staff meeting and listening to a coworker present information on the legal use of copyrighted images Darrell realizes some of the information may not be accurate What should he do?
choices: Ask for permission to bring the companys attorney to the meeting
Explain that the information is incorrect
Ask questions to clarify the information
Dont say anything because it would embarrass his coworker
explanation: Ask questions to clarify the information. It is better to ask a question to clarify information than to point out that someone is wrong. Besides, Darrell may not be aware of recent changes in copyright law. Inviting another person to a meeting to prove his point would be considered rude, and others might doubt his ability to trust their judgment or support them in the future. It's important to avoid embarrassing coworkers, but if Darrell has valid concerns, politely sharing them is the best course of action.

prompt: Customer complaints can eat into a businesss profits by
choices: forcing it to sell returned items at reduced prices
explanation: Forcing it to sell returned items at reduced prices. Customer complaints can eat into a business's profits by forcing it to sell returned items at reduced prices. When a complaint can't be resolved and a customer returns an item, it is unlikely that the business will recover the full amount of expected profit. Unhappy employees do not necessarily affect profitability. An increase in sales volume would likely boost profitability, not cause it to go down. Customer complaints do not necessarily cause a business to reduce its marketing budget.

prompt: An organizations structure should ensure that customers experiences with the business are
explanation: Seamless. An organization's structure should ensure that customers' experiences with the business are seamless. This can sometimes be difficult because different departments may have different methods of reaching business goals. Departments must work together to keep CRM a priority. Businesses want customer experiences to result in profit, but organizational structure does not necessarily ensure this. Businesses do not want customers' experiences to be endless or time-consuming.

prompt: Societies must determine how to allocate resources between production of __________ and __________ goods
explanation: Capital goods; consumer. Because resources are limited, they must be divided between capital and consumer goods. Natural resources are not produced. Individuals as well as businesses consume services.

prompt: Which of the following makes globalization more difficult
explanation: Terrorist threats. Terrorist threats can make globalization more difficult and costly. International trade is dampened when the safety of people and operations is in question. Stronger infrastructures, new technologies, and faster transportation are all factors that aid globalization.

prompt: Why are consumer goods often poor quality in a communist command economy?
choices: People in a communist command economy consume everything that they produce
People in a communist command economy do not need quality consumer goods
High taxes take resources away from producers
The government pays workers based on quantity rather than quality
explanation: The government pays workers based on quantity rather than quality. In a communist command economy, most resources are allocated toward industrial goods rather than consumer goods. The few consumer goods that are available are often poor quality because the government pays workers based on the quantity, not the quality, of what they produce. People in communist command economies need consumer goods as much as those in other economic systems do. High taxes do not necessarily have a direct effect on production of consumer goods. Finally, people in a communist command economy do not consume everything that they produce; this is instead a characteristic of a traditional economy.

prompt: Which of the following should be included in GDP
choices: A tractor purchased by a farmer to use for his crops
Wheat sold to a baker for his bread
Cement used to build a new office building
explanation: A tractor purchased by a farmer to use for his crops. A tractor that a farmer purchases to use for his crops is an example of gross private domestic investment. Gross private domestic investment includes purchases by the business sector and is included in GDP. It is a capital good that the farmer uses in his business. Wheat that a baker purchases to make bread, which he then sells to customers, should not be included in GDP because it is an intermediate product. Intermediate products are those that are part of other finished products. Cement used to build a new office building is also an intermediate product. Intermediate products should not be counted because they would overinflate GDP. Government welfare payments are not included in GDP because they are transfer payments, which are payments of tax dollars to recipients who have not produced goods or services.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason that a company might decide to offer credit
explanation: To gain new customers. All businesses lose customers from time to time due to factors such as relocation, illness or death, or loss of employment. Therefore, to be successful, businesses must continually attract new customers. One way to do this is by offering credit. Convenience, saving money, and purchasing expensive items are all benefits that businesses or consumers may get from using credit. Offering credit will likely not be convenient for a business, and it will probably cost the business more money.

prompt: Nala who is preparing a personal budget is determining her fixed and variable expenses Which of the following is most likely to represent a fixed expense
explanation: Car payment. Car payments are typically set up as a fixed monthly payment amount. Electric bills can vary depending on the amount of energy used. The amount spent on groceries can vary greatly depending on the types of food purchased. The amount spent on gasoline would vary depending on the amount of travel.

prompt: Kevin has been instructed to do marketing research for his company on a recently released product Before he begins he asks his manager what kind of data he should gather how much data to gather and how the data will be used In other words Kevin would like to know the research
explanation: Objectives. Research objectives state exactly what the research study will achieve, including what kind of data will be gathered, how much data will be gathered, and how the data will be used. A research problem explains the issue or concern that researchers hope to gain clarity on through research. A research question is an inquiry that the researchers hope to answer during their research activities, and a research hypothesis is the assumption or "educated guess" to that question (usually specified as an "if, then" statement).

prompt: Kaitlin is working on a research project for her college marketing course She creates a survey and distributes it to every student living in her dorm What type of sample design is Kaitlin using?
explanation: Convenience sampling. Convenience sampling is a type of non-probability sampling that collects data from people who are conveniently available. Judgment sampling requires researchers to "handpick" respondents based on their knowledge or expertise. Quota sampling ensures that specific groups within a target population will be represented within the sample. Snowball sampling, also called referral sampling, is a method in which researchers ask respondents to help them identify and recruit additional respondents for the study. Kaitlin did not handpick respondents, target specific groups, or ask respondents to identify other respondents--she simply distributed her survey to the students conveniently available to her.

prompt: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the experiment method of data collection
choices: Experiments are prone to technical difficulties
Experiments do not show cause and effect
Experiments can be difficult to design for marketing purposes
explanation: Experiments can be difficult to design for marketing purposes. Experiments can be difficult to design for marketing purposes since marketers must take human behavior (which is very complex) into account. Experiments do, however, show cause and effect. They are not necessarily prone to technical difficulties and do not necessarily raise concerns about privacy.

prompt: Neutral survey items are simple non threatening questions that establish rapport and put the respondent at ease Neutral questions should be placed
choices: in a separate post survey questionnaire
in the middle of the survey
at the end of the survey
at the beginning of the survey
explanation: At the beginning of the survey. By establishing rapport early on, respondents will be more comfortable answering more probing questions later in the survey. Neutral questions should not be placed at the middle, at the end, or in a separate post-survey questionnaire--their effect would be significantly reduced.

prompt: When Rebeccas research for her school project is complete shes not quite sure what to do with her data Her friend Allison suggests coding the data and she decides to give it a try Why should Rebecca use coding to organize her research findings?
choices: It is the only method to interpret data in a meaningful way
It turns large amounts of data into a form that is more easily understood
It prevents data entry mistakes such as omissions or duplications
It saves time by eliminating the need to check the data for flaws and errors
explanation: It turns large amounts of data into a form that is more easily understood. To make sense of large amounts of data, the data must be analyzed. Coding can be an extremely useful tool for data analysis by grouping and assigning value to various responses from the survey. While coding is one way to interpret data in a meaningful way, it is not the only way. Coding does not prevent data entry mistakes. In many cases, it is still humans who assign the coding system and manually enter codes into a computer--there is always the possibility of human error. Data should always be checked for flaws at multiple points during the analysis. Coding should not be used as a replacement for error checking.

prompt: Ben is trying to figure out how his classmates feel about a new dress code policy at school so he decides to do some research on the issue What type of research is most appropriate for his research question?
explanation: Primary, qualitative research. Primary research involves direct interaction with subjects through focus groups, interviews, or surveys to create original and unique information. Secondary research involves sifting through readily available information through Internet research, books, former primary research studies, and more. Qualitative research is better for uncovering personal opinions, beliefs, values and other non-numerical information, whereas quantitative research collects numerical data that are used to uncover statistical trends. Because Ben is investigating the feelings and attitudes of his classmates, it makes the most sense for him to conduct primary, qualitative research.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of marketing an idea
choices: Concert sponsored by a soft drink company
Sports star promoting his new line of shoes
explanation: Campaign against texting while driving. A campaign against texting while driving is marketing the idea that texting while driving is dangerous and should be stopped. A poster for a school dance is marketing an event. A concert sponsored by a soft drink company is marketing an event and a good. A sports star promoting his new line of shoes is marketing a person and a good.

prompt: A marketer is trying to figure out what the companys customers need and how the company can meet those needs Which element of the marketing mix is this marketer working on?
explanation: Product. The product element of the marketing mix involves the goods, services, or ideas a business will offer its customers. Marketers conduct research and use their creativity to figure out what customers need and how they will meet those needs. Place, price, and promotion are other elements of the marketing mix.

prompt: Jake is a high school soccer player who is about to begin the fall season While he is getting ready for his first practice he realizes that his cleats from last year are too small and that he needs to buy a new pair The soccer specialty store near Jakes house would consider Jake to be a member of its
explanation: Target market. A target market is the particular group of customers a business seeks to attract. Jake is a soccer player with a need for new cleats—he fits the target market for a soccer specialty store perfectly. A market segment is more specific—it is one of the groups into which the total target market is divided. For example, female goalkeepers and male defenders are both market segments within the larger target population of soccer players. An industrial market includes customers or potential customers who purchase items for use in the operation of a business, for resale, or for making other goods. Geographic segmentation is the division of a market on the basis of where customers are located.

prompt: Which of the following situations is an example of how external factors could affect a companys marketing situation
choices: A candy company enters a joint venture with an international partner
A shoe manufacturer releases a new line of athletic gear
A recent health care law affects procedures at a hospital
A technology firm hires a new president
explanation: A recent health care law affects procedures at a hospital. The situation analysis must discuss the climate, or external factors, that could affect the marketing situation. External factors can be social and cultural, demographic, economic, technological, or political and legal. A new health care law is an example of a political and legal change that would affect the marketing efforts of a hospital. A shoe company releasing a new line of athletic gear is an internal company change, as is a technology firm hiring a new president. A joint venture is an example of a collaboration, rather than an external factor.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement regarding the effect of the product life cycle on a businesss sales forecast
choices: Anticipated sales remain the same throughout the product life cycle
At the end of the product life cycle anticipated sales are low
Anticipated sales are lowest during the growth phase of the product life cycle
During the maturity phase of the product life cycle anticipated sales are extremely high
explanation: At the end of the product life cycle, anticipated sales are low. Anticipated sales for a product change as the product progresses through the product life cycle. During the growth phase, anticipated sales are high. During the maturity phase, sales begin to slow down. As a product is "dying," anticipated sales are generally quite low (e.g., demand for VCRs as DVD players were being introduced).

prompt: Information management can help a business protect its customers from
explanation: Receiving spam messages. Information management can help a business protect its customers from receiving spam messages (repetitive or unwanted messages). Information management cannot necessarily prevent customers from experiencing buyers' remorse, having items broken during shipping, or dealing with discourteous employees.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement regarding the effect of technology on business
choices: Technology has allowed almost every U S employee to telecommute
Technology has lessened competition among businesses
explanation: Technology can spawn new industries. New technologies can create new industries. Examples include the aviation industry and the robotics industry. Technology has increased employees' ability to telecommute--but only about 50 percent of American workers do so. Technology has also lowered production costs and increased competition among businesses.

prompt: The local movie theater is experiencing a decline in business because a new zoo attraction is drawing record crowds What type of competition is the theater experiencing?
explanation: Substitute. A theater and a zoo are different types of entertainment, so the theater is experiencing substitute competition. Brand competition is competition among similar products of different brands. General competition involves all businesses competing for scarce customer dollars. Direct competition is rivalry between businesses that offer similar types of goods or services.

prompt: Which of the following situations is a conflict of interest
choices: An employee fails to report a safety violation
A purchasing employee receives gifts from a supplier
A manager monitors her his employees emails
A business sells products that have nearly expired
explanation: A purchasing employee receives gifts from a supplier. When an employee receives gifts from a supplier or potential supplier, it can present a conflict of interest, or a situation in which the employee is unable to make a truly impartial decision. Conflicts of interest do not necessarily occur when an employee fails to report a safety violation, when a manager monitors her/his employees' emails, or when a business sells products that have nearly expired.

prompt: Which of the following is an accurate statement concerning a projects budget
choices: If a companys resources are used equipment costs can be disregarded
When estimating the cost of a project labor costs are not included
Projects are experiments and not expected to make a profit
A project budget should include funds to cover unexpected costs
explanation: A project budget should include funds to cover unexpected costs. Project managers often encounter unexpected costs while completing their projects, so funds should be included in the budget for such expenses. Labor costs are typically included in a project's cost. Projects may involve experimenting with a new approach or product, but they are still expected to turn a profit. If a project requires use of a company's equipment, the cost of using that equipment should be included in the project budget.

prompt: Which of the following is most likely to positively impact both productivity and quality
choices: Precut materials to reduce production time
Materials with the lowest possible cost
Quality materials that arrive on time
explanation: Quality materials that arrive on time. Two purchasing-related factors that can have a significant impact on quality and productivity are the quality of the materials and the timeliness of their delivery. High quality materials only benefit productivity if they arrive on time. Inexpensive materials may decrease the cost of goods sold, but they aren't likely to increase productivity and quality. Materials that are precut to reduce production time could increase productivity, but only if they are delivered on time. Precut materials may or may not increase the quality of the outputs.

prompt: Which of the following is the best thing for a manager to do to create a culture of quality in the workplace
choices: Hold a department meeting highlighting the need for quality work
Reward employees for making suggestions to improve quality
Put up motivational signs that state that quality is everyones job
Discourage errors by holding employees accountable for their actions
explanation: Reward employees for making suggestions to improve quality. Management as well as front-line employees should be involved in creating a quality culture. While holding a meeting or putting up motivational signs tells employees what is expected of them, rewarding them for making suggestions to improve quality is more likely to contribute to a culture of quality in the workplace. To create a culture of quality, managers should focus on improving processes instead of pointing out employees' mistakes.

prompt: Shonda needs to choose between two colleges After doing a lot of research about both schools she has a gut feeling that one is the right choice so she decides to go there Shonda is using __________ to solve her problem
explanation: Intuition. Intuitive problem solving relies on "gut" feelings and flashes of insight. Shonda does research on both colleges, but it's her intuition that helps her ultimately decide between them. The seven-step method, brainstorming, and mind mapping are all ways to solve problems, but Shonda is not using any of them in this example.

prompt: A pet food manufacturing company has decided to remove all non meat fillers from its pet food by the end of the fiscal year This is an example of a n
explanation: Goal. A goal is a specific, desired accomplishment over a defined period of time. An organization's mission is the reason behind its establishment--what it is meant to do or produce. Objectives are statements of broad intent that often arise out of mission statements. A strategy is a general course of action for meeting objectives, taking into account the current situation and available resources.

prompt: Which of the following is a job duty for a merchandiser buyer
explanation: Negotiating with vendors. Merchandisers and buyers have many job duties, including keeping up with trends, analyzing sales, negotiating with vendors, and predicting what will sell in the future. Public relations professionals write press releases, advertisers design advertisements, and marketing research professionals organize focus groups.

prompt: Before a good can be sold the buyers and sellers first have to agree on a n
explanation: Exchange price. An exchange price is the amount of money that the buyer is willing to pay and the seller is willing to accept for a good or service. A market share is an organization's portion of the total industry sales in a specific market. Promotion decisions refer to the selection of the various types of communications that marketers use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of their products. Pricing objectives are goals a company hopes to accomplish through its pricing strategies.

prompt: Melissa is eager to visit a local department store after seeing an advertisement for a great deal on new mattresses When she gets to the store however the salesperson explains that the on sale model quickly sold out and attempts to sell her a much more expensive mattress This is an example of
explanation: Bait-and-switch advertising. Bait-and-switch advertising is an unethical and fraudulent sales method in which a store advertises extremely low prices, and then attempts to sell customers different products at higher prices once they visit the store. The purpose of the tactic is to get customers to visit a business in the hopes that they will make a purchase, even if it's not the exact item that they wanted. Predatory pricing is the act of setting prices low in an attempt to eliminate the competition. Price discrimination occurs when a business charges different customers different prices for similar amounts and types of products. Price fixing is an agreement among competitors to "fix," or set the price, for a product so that it is the same among all the stores. All of these methods are unethical and illegal.

prompt: After increasing its products price so that it is higher than a competing products price the Expert Companys profits have begun decreasing What is most likely happening?
choices: The company is selling more products at the higher price point
The company is being perceived as having a discount image
Customers dont think the product is worth more than a competing product
The company is undercutting competitors pricing to sell more products
explanation: Customers don't think the product is worth more than a competing product. If a company increases the product price and profits are decreasing, most likely customers do not think the product's value is worth more than that of a competing product. The company may be seen as having an exclusive image with the higher price point. If profits are decreasing, the company is selling less product than before the price change. The company is not undercutting competitor's pricing--it is selling above competitor's prices.

prompt: A products sales have been slowly declining over the past year A superior product was introduced to the market and now the original product is unable to compete What process should the products company carry out?
explanation: Product discontinuation. Weak products are those with declining sales and profitability. These products must be discontinued because of their costs to the company. Commercialization is the point at which the product goes into full-scale production, a marketing plan is put in place, service and sales training are conducted, and the product's life cycle begins. Product development is a lengthy step that could take months or even years to finish. During this step, a working model of the product is tested, modified, and retested, until the company decides it's ready to hit the market. Companies create prototypes when they are testing a product concept, not when a product is already on the market and unsuccessful.

prompt: Kelly runs a successful start up company that sells homemade nut butters After several months of explosive growth she notices that her sales seem to have peaked Her products are still selling but at a slower rate than before Kellys products are in the __________ stage of the product life cycle
explanation: Maturity. The maturity stage is the product life cycle stage in which sales peak and then increase at a slower rate or start to decline. The growth stage is the stage in which sales rise rapidly, whereas the decline stage is the stage in which sales decrease and profits begin to erode. The introduction stage is the stage in which the product first appears in the marketplace.

prompt: A new change to educational policy increases the number of math classes that students need to take to graduate A textbook publisher then creates a new line of instructional materials based on these changes This is an example of how
choices: companies need to pay better attention to customer feedback
economic changes are detrimental to product development
competitors are a useful source of product innovation
explanation: Political trends create product opportunities. Trends and changes in the political sphere sometimes create new product opportunities and open new markets. If educational policy changes allow a textbook publisher to create a new line of instructional materials, the policy created a product opportunity. This is not an example of how economic changes are detrimental to new product development, how competitors are a useful source of product innovation, or of how companies need to pay better attention to customer feedback.

prompt: Dana owns a restaurant that specializes in burgers and fries After experiencing success Dana decided to add milkshakes to the menu because she thought they would go well with the other menu items The milkshakes burgers and fries are examples of __________ goods
explanation: Complementary. A complementary good is one that goes with something else. Milkshakes can be added to burgers and fries as a beverage or dessert option to complete the meal. Specialty goods are goods that are unique enough that customers are willing to put forth special effort to obtain them. Milkshakes do not fit into this category because they are fairly ordinary. A substitute good is one that replaces another because it satisfies the same need or want. Milkshakes are not replacing one of Dana's current products. Finally, a trend-driven good is one that is inspired by a current trend in society or in a particular industry. There is no indication that the decision to add milkshakes was based on a trend.

prompt: Geoff doesnt waste materials at his job He is helping his company meet __________ standards
explanation: Cost. Cost standards are used to specify project or product costs. They are important because the measure of a business's success is profit. Increased costs, without a proportionate increase in sales, decreases profit. Wasting material or taking more time than necessary to perform a task adds to the cost of doing business. This is not an example of helping his company meet time, quality, or quantity standards.

prompt: Which of the following data might be included on a warranty card or registration
choices: Sales in relation to prior time periods
explanation: Where the product was purchased. A warranty card or registration can be a valuable source of secondary data for a business. It includes information about where the product was purchased. Warranty cards do not contain competitor information, prospects contacted (contained on a call report), or data about sales in relation to prior time periods (contained on a sales report.)

prompt: Consumer protection laws benefit businesses by
explanation: Protecting them from financial losses. Consumer protection laws also benefit businesses because they protect businesses from financial losses caused by consumer lawsuits, government fines, and defective or unsafe products that cannot be sold. Preventing injuries and illness, combating consumer faults, and simplifying buying decisions are all benefits to consumers, rather than to businesses.

prompt: A fast food restaurant decides to add a new line of salads to its menu The company is using a n ___________ product mix strategy
explanation: Expansion. A business may expand its product mix by adding additional product items or lines. There are a number of reasons why a business may choose an expansion product-mix strategy, including satisfying customers' desire for variety, offering customers complementary products, spreading risk over a wider area, appealing to a new market, increasing sales and profits, enhancing the company's reputation, and making more efficient use of the company facilities. Contraction means removing product items or lines from the product mix. When a company decides to add a higher priced product or line to its mix, it is using a trading-up strategy. When a company decides to add a lower priced product or line to its mix, it is using a trading-down strategy.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit customers receive from product bundling
explanation: Convenience. Product bundling is when two products are sold together as one item or purchase. It is convenient for customers because they have fewer separate purchases to make and can obtain several items that they need at once. Product bundling can increase revenue for businesses rather than for customers. Access to unpopular products is not a benefit for customers. Improved workflow is a benefit for business rather than for customers.

prompt: Jill only buys Natural Glow cosmetics and will go from store to store until she finds them Jill is in the brand __________ stage of brand loyalty
explanation: Insistence. Brand insistence has been achieved when a consumer refuses alternative products and searches exclusively for the desired merchandise. In this case, Jill insists upon Natural Glow cosmetics and makes sure she buys them over any other brand of cosmetics. Brand evangelism occurs when you are an advocate for a brand, convincing others that the brand is the best. In this case, there is no indication that Jill is a brand evangelist for Natural Glow. Brand preference occurs when you prefer a brand based on previous experience with it and will select it over competitors when the option is available. In this case, Jill is beyond the level of brand preference because she only wants Natural Glow, even when it is not available. Brand recognition means that the consumer is aware of and can identify a brand. Jill is beyond this point with Natural Glow.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of using customer voice to build your brand
choices: Blocking all negative social media posts that customers write about your brand
Posting positive customer reviews prominently on your website
Promoting the best selling products that you already know customers love
Letting customers spread the word about your brand to their friends and family
explanation: Posting positive customer reviews prominently on your website. Customer feedback is a great way to promote your brand as positive and trustworthy. You should prominently display your best customer reviews on your website so prospective customers will develop a positive attitude toward your brand. Blocking all negative social media posts that customers might write about your brand will make you seem untrustworthy and dishonest. It is better to address these complaints. Promoting the best-selling products that you already know customers love does not involve using customer voice. Finally, letting customers spread the word about your brand is not actively using customer voice to promote or build your brand.

prompt: A companys strategy culture and communication combine to form brand
explanation: Identity. Brand identity is the culmination of what a company wants to be--what it says about who it is. Strategy, culture, and communication all contribute to brand identity. Brand touchpoints are any instances in which the customers encounter the brand, such as a promotional message or a company website. Brand cues are messages that affect buying behavior in regard to a brand, such as a certain word that makes a customer think of a product. A brand promise is a commitment made by a brand to its customers about what it intends to deliver.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a customer touchpoint that is important during the purchase stage
explanation: A retail store. Touchpoints are any interactions a business has with customers. Touchpoints give customers the opportunity to form an opinion of the brand. When a customer is making a purchase, a retail store is a touchpoint that a customer might encounter. Product reviews are more likely to be a factor during the pre-purchase stage. Customer service teams are likely to be a touchpoint during the postpurchase phase. A charity sponsorship is more likely to be important during the pre-purchase stage.

prompt: You see a billboard advertising beef from the Cattlemens Beef Board This is an example of __________ product promotion
explanation: Primary. Primary product promotion aims to stimulate demand, or desire, for an entire class of goods or services. The emphasis is on the product and its uses, rather than on a particular brand. When you see an advertisement for beef from the Cattlemen's Beef Board, you are receiving a primary promotional message. Secondary, or selective, product promotion is used to stimulate demand for a specific brand of a product. Public-service promotions inform customers about noncontroversial issues that are in the public's best interest. Public-relations promotion is a type of institutional promotion created to deal with controversial public issues that are related to a company or its products.

prompt: Will wants to open a food truck business but he lives in a city where many other food trucks already operate Will should
choices: set up meetings with potential customers to explain his business
run a local radio ad that explains why his food truck is different
perform charitable activities so he will receive positive publicity
explanation: Run a local radio ad that explains why his food truck is different. Advertisements are an effective promotional strategy when a product needs to be differentiated from its competitors, as well as when a product is in its introductory stage. Therefore, a radio ad that focuses on differentiating Will's food truck from others is an appropriate tactic. Setting up meetings with potential customers to explain his business is not an effective strategy for Will because personal selling is not generally used for convenience goods such as food. Will would not be able to meet with enough customers to make his business profitable. Performing charitable activities to receive good publicity would be more effective when Will has already established his brand. It is hard to generate publicity during the introductory stage. Finally, a merchandising allowance is a sales promotion that is used when promoting to intermediary businesses, rather than directly to consumers, as is the case with Will's food truck.

prompt: Which of the following examples depicts an advantage of using digital advertising
choices: Conversion rates of banner ads are more difficult to measure than in print
Ethan uses ad blocking software so he can stream videos commercial free
Viewers must interact with a video ad before continuing to a website
Digital ads are more expensive than television advertisements
explanation: Viewers must interact with a video ad before continuing to a website. One of the biggest challenges facing any advertisement is engagement--keeping the viewers' attention and making sure they are receiving the message. It is easy for viewers to ignore video ads, either digital or traditional, but if they are forced to interact with the ad in some way, they are more likely to pay attention to the ad and take in its message. Ad-blocking software is a disadvantage to digital advertising, rather than an advantage. Conversion rates are easier to measure online than in print. Finally, digital ads are generally cheaper than television advertisements.

prompt: Which of the following advertisements is most likely to violate promotional regulations
choices: A toy commercial uses bright colors and a catchy jingle
A food advertisement depicts a child using a stove unsupervised
An email newsletter includes an opt out link at the bottom
The people in a prescription drug commercial are designated as actors
explanation: A food advertisement depicts a child using a stove unsupervised. Advertisements that are unfair or cause injury to consumers can violate consumer protection regulations. An advertisement that shows a child using the stove unsupervised can be dangerous to children who might see the advertisement and think it's okay for them to use the stove by themselves. A toy commercial that uses bright colors and a catchy jingle would not necessarily violate any regulation. Email newsletters should always include an opt-out link so that they don't violate regulation. Finally, a prescription drug commercial should clarify that the people in it are actors, rather than actual users of the drug.

prompt: A local pizza place gives you a magnet that includes its logo website and phone number This is an example of
explanation: Specialty media. Specialty media is a type of "other" media that features a business's logo, is useful, and is given away freely. A magnet featuring a business's logo, website, and phone number is considered specialty media. Directory advertising includes promotional messages found in directories of a general nature such as the Yellow Pages or in specialized listings of companies in an industry. Product placement is a type of "other" media that uses products as props in movies, television shows, and video games. A spectacular is a type of out-of-home advertisement built to order and often designed with neon lights or moving parts.

prompt: Which of the following is an important component of a businesss press kit
explanation: Biographies of key company figures. A press kit is a package of information about a company, whether physical or digital, that is sent out to reporters in hopes of generating interest about that company. The press kit should be a “one-stop shop” of all information a reporter could need to write about the company. This includes biographies of key figures in the company, such as the CEO, COO, etc. Promotional messages, interviews, and customer testimonials are not necessarily important components of a press kit.

prompt: What is the first requirement for writing successful advertising copy?
explanation: Grab attention. If an ad's copy does not grab a reader's attention, it will never be seen, read, or understood. Therefore, a piece of copy must first and foremost attract attention. Being informative, persuading readers, and demanding action are all important but are not the first priorities. Attention must be captured first before any of these requirements can be achieved.

prompt: A furniture store released an ad in the weekly paper but readers complained that it was too busy and difficult to know where to focus The advertisement should have included more
explanation: White space. White space is essential because it separates images on the page, keeps the page from looking cluttered and messy, and makes the advertisement clearer. White space could help the furniture store's ad to look less busy. More fonts would probably make the ad look busier and would not necessarily help the readers know where to focus. Logos and graphics would not necessarily help the ad to be less busy.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a one way public relations activity that could be used to distribute company information directly to the target audience
explanation: Newsletters. Newsletters are one-way communications from the company to its target audience that contain important information about the company. They can be sent via email or through regular mail. Search engine optimization is a tactic used to boost an organization's ability to be discovered through search engine tools. It is not a direct way of distributing information to the target audience; rather, it is a strategy that can be employed in many types of PR content. Press conferences and social media are not one-way public relations activities; rather, they are interactive.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a tangible product
explanation: A pizza. Pizza is a tangible product because it can be detected by the senses. Tangible products can be touched, smelled, tasted, seen, or heard. An insurance policy, cooking lessons, and a haircut are all intangible products because they are services you could pay someone else to perform. You cannot detect intangible objects through the senses.

prompt: Joaquin a car salesman is sure to send out a personalized thank you note every time he makes a sale Which key to customer service is he demonstrating?
explanation: Keeping in touch. Good salespeople recognize that keeping in contact with customers is one of the best ways to maintain their partnerships. Sometimes this involves sending out a thank-you note, as in Joaquin's case. Sometimes this can be as simple as a follow-up phone call, or for major clients, it may even involve a personal visit. Soliciting feedback, being prompt, and having a good attitude are all important keys to customer service, but Joaquin is not demonstrating them in this example.

prompt: Elizabeth is looking for a new laptop for college She visits a technology store finds a computer that she likes and asks the salesperson about the warranty on the laptop Elizabeth is asking about the stores __________ policy
explanation: Guarantee. These types of policies are guarantees of quality or product performance and often include warranties which cover a certain period of time or specific parts of the product. Repair and maintenance policies are policies that offer continued care of a product for a specified or indefinite amount of time. Companies who offer potentially dangerous products or services (parasailing or bungee jumping, for example) may have a liability policy that requires salespeople to obtain a liability waiver from the customer. These waivers release the company from responsibility for something that might go wrong. Return and adjustment policies govern the return of goods, including how and when customers can return products.

prompt: Which of the following sales actions is considered illegal
choices: A salesperson ignores his her coworkers unethical actions
An employer puts too much pressure on his her sales employees
A salesperson says something untrue that damages a competitors business
A salesperson takes a client out to dinner
explanation: A salesperson says something untrue that damages a competitor's business. When you say something untrue that damages a person's or business's reputation, that's considered slander, which is illegal. An employer putting too much pressure on his/her sales employees and a salesperson ignoring his/her coworker's misbehavior are both considered unethical actions, but they aren't illegal. A salesperson taking a client out to dinner is not typically considered unethical or illegal, although if a salesperson isn't careful, s/he could cross over into the legal issue of bribery.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement regarding the use of product information for selling
choices: It is impossible to give customers too much product information
Salespeople should not rely on selling skills alone
It is not necessary to acquire information about the industry as a whole
Salespeople should rely on technical language when sharing product information
explanation: Salespeople should not rely on selling skills alone. It is important to acquire product information for answering customers' questions, demonstrating how the product meets their needs, etc. Selling skills alone will not result in sales success. Sometimes, it is possible to overwhelm customers by giving them too much information or by using too much technical jargon. It is important for salespeople to acquire industry information as well as product information.

prompt: Which of the following statements describes features
choices: They answer the question Whats in it for me?
They can be obvious exclusive or hidden
They are the advantages a customer wants from a product
explanation: They are physical characteristics. A feature is a physical characteristic or quality of a product. It is something the customer can touch, feel, smell, see, or measure. It helps to describe the product. In short, a feature answers the question, "What is it?" Benefits, not features, can be obvious, exclusive, or hidden. Benefits are the advantages a customer wants from a product, and they answer the question, "What's in it for me?"

prompt: In what stage of the selling process do salespeople handle objections?
explanation: Reaching closure. Closing a sale often has two distinct parts or steps--overcoming objections and getting the order. Clearing up objections can serve as a chance for the salesperson to demonstrate his/her knowledge and further solidify the product's benefits to the customer. Prescribing solutions to a customer's needs involves making product suggestions based on a customer's specific situation, and occurs after the salesperson has determined the customer's needs through questioning. Reaffirming the buyer-seller relationship occurs after a sale has been made, when the salesperson reassures the customer that they have made a good purchase decision. Preparing to sell is the very first phase of the selling process, and involves preliminary research and planning the sales presentation.
